Open source hardware for your Muse

Muse gadgets are open source devices you build yourself. Program an off-the-shelf ESP32 board or set up a Raspberry Pi with our SDKs, then connect Muse to your displays, buttons, sensors, actuators, and whatever else you’ve got lying on your workbench.

01 / ON YOUR HARDWARE

Make your own

We open sourced the code you need to make a Muse gadget. It’s built by hackers, for hackers, just for fun. Side effects of tinkering may include bricked boards, voided warranties, brownouts, or bankruptcies. Proceed at your own risk!

Get started by grabbing an SDK token and one of our featured project ideas. Then tinker and customize to your heart’s delight. Or build support for an entirely new board if that’s more your thing.

ESP32 Device SDK↗

Connect your ESP32 board to Muse through our open source SDK. Throw in a screen to show images, add audio in and out, or wire up other sensors.

Linux Device SDK↗

Turn that spare Raspberry Pi or Linux box into a Muse gadget. Hack in your own commands to let Muse handle sysadmin chores or your Home Assistant setup.

Source

Explore the source code for our device SDKs and firmware. Use it as a starting point for your projects and contribute your improvements back to the community.

02 / USE OUR HARDWARE

One we made: Muse Home Link

Connect Muse to your home Wi-Fi so it can reach compatible devices you already own, or anything you build with a local HTTP API. Community-built skills can let Muse turn on a light, control your TV, send a document to a printer, and more, depending on your setup.

Claim your Muse Home Link↗

Free with an active Muse subscription in the United States only, limit one per subscriber. Ships in October, first come, first served.

Share your project

Made a Muse Gadget? Share it in #projects on Discord. We may feature it here, linked to your repo so others can build it.

Before you post

  1. Capture a photo or short video.
  2. Write a line or two about your project.
  3. Have a GitHub repo with a README ready.
